explanation: The theorem is about this library's own definition `MvPolynomial.ZariskiSpace.zeroLocus I` (a set of the wrapped tuple type `ZariskiSpace K σ`, defined as `{x | x.toFun ∈ MvPolynomial.zeroLocus K I}`) in the topology induced by `pointToPoint`. Mathlib has no `ZariskiSpace` and no statement that this wrapped zero locus is closed. The nearest Mathlib results are `MvPolynomial.zeroLocus` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Nullstellensatz.lean, just a definition of a set of functions with no topology at all, hence no closedness lemma) and `PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_zeroLocus` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Topology.lean:156), which concerns a different set in the prime spectrum of an arbitrary commutative semiring. Deriving the library statement would require proving the set equality `ZariskiSpace.zeroLocus I = pointToPoint ⁻¹' PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus I` (via `zariskiIdeal_le`/`mem_vanishingIdeal_singleton_iff`) and using continuity of the induced map, which is more than the permitted one- or two-line glue and is essentially the library's own content; the current proof itself goes through the library's `isClosed_iff`. I also grepped Mathlib for `zeroLocus`/`isClosed_zeroLocus` in the spectrum, scheme and ringed-space sources and found no matching declaration.
